transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I... I just don't know what else to do at this point. I'm here because, well, I work as a bookkeeping clerk. I got the job right out of high school and I used to really like it, but now it's just completely taking over my life. 

I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. Like, I'll finish a ledger, and I know I finished it, but I just have to check it. And then I check it again. And again. It's gotten so severe that I'm staying at work for hours and hours after everyone else leaves for the day. The whole office will be completely empty, the lights are off in the hallway, the cleaning crew has already come and gone, and I'm just sitting there at my desk re-adding the exact same column of numbers even though I already checked them ten times. 

Because... well, if I don't do it just one more time, I get this overwhelming, heavy feeling that something incredibly bad is going to happen. Like the company's accounts will be ruined, or someone will get in huge legal trouble, and it will be entirely my fault because I missed a single decimal point. I know I already checked it, but I just can't shake that feeling that it's going to be my fault if I don't look just one more time to be absolutely sure. So I just keep checking and checking until I'm so exhausted I can barely see the screen, and I just... I can't stop doing it.
Do you ever have upsetting thoughts, images, or impulses that come into your mind repeatedly, even when you try to ignore them, that make you feel very anxious or uncomfortable?

Yes, that is exactly it. It's like... well, it's exactly what you just said. I'll be sitting there, and I literally just ran the calculator tape, right? I have the physical paper right next to the keyboard, and I can clearly see that the numbers match. The accounts perfectly balance. But then, right as I go to close the spreadsheet or put the folder in the outbox, this thought just jumps into my head. 

It's this loud, awful thought that I missed one tiny, hidden mistake somewhere deep in the rows. Like, especially when I'm dealing with payroll or the quarterly taxes. I'll start thinking, "What if I transposed a number on someone's direct deposit?" And then my mind just completely spirals. I start picturing that somebody's paycheck won't go through on Friday, and then they won't be able to pay their rent or buy groceries, and they'll be evicted, all because I messed up one digit. Or I'll get this flashing image that the firm is going to get audited and get in this massive, catastrophic trouble with the government. 

And I try so, so hard to just push the thought away, I really do. I tell myself, "You just checked this, it's fine, just get up and go home." I'll even close my eyes and physically shake my head to try and clear the thought out. But it just comes right back, instantly. It just pounds at me and pounds at me until my chest feels tight. It's like... it's like I completely lose the ability to trust my own eyes. I can be staring right at the correct number on the screen, but the thought that it's actually wrong and everything is going to be ruined is just so intense and uncomfortable that I can't ignore it. I just have to open the file back up. I just can't make those thoughts stop coming, no matter what I do.

Other candidates (F43.22, F41.1) are ruled out based on the presence of clear obsessive and compulsive behaviors beyond general anxiety or adjustment issues.
